propositions: Plan-review PASS verdicts do not persist a signed attestation by default on all mutating public routes, despite incurring full LLM cost and leaving the ticket indistinguishable from unsigned for subsequent claim-gate validation.

Every mutating plan-review entry point (CLI review-plan, library review_plan) must sign and persist a claim-valid attestation by default when the verdict is a non-degraded PASS; explicit opt-out requires --no-sign (CLI) or sign=False (library).

BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, degraded, and explicitly unsigned results must never sign; sign_plan_review must enforce these guards at the shared finalization seam so they are pinned at the artifact owning the policy.
Re-running a default plan-review operation with a current claim-valid attestation must reuse it without an LLM call or duplicate signature event.
A PASS whose signature persistence fails must return a retryable nonzero disposition and identify sign-review as the recovery path instead of reporting success.
Documentation and CLI help must state the sign-on-PASS default, name the explicit --no-sign exception, and describe non-signable verdicts and sign-review recovery.
